metadata.title: ICT use predicts reading literacy: a serial multiple mediation model of reading enjoyment and metacognition based on PISA 2018 data

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses the Hong Kong sample from PISA 2018, which is drawn using a two-stage stratified and proportional design at the school level followed by an online survey of sampled 15-year-old students. PISA assigns sampling weights to both students and schools to account for sampling errors and measurement errors, but the manuscript does not report the specific weight variables used in the authors’ SPSS/PROCESS mediation and regression analyses. Because the analysis is based on standard regression/bootstrapped mediation in SPSS (PROCESS 3.3) rather than IEA/OECD replicate-weight procedures, it is unclear whether complex survey weighting was applied. Analysts using the PISA 2018 database should apply the appropriate student and school weights (and replicate methods if available) when estimating standard errors and confidence intervals to better reflect the clustered sampling design.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the Hong Kong sample from PISA 2018. The authors retained only students who completed both the student questionnaire and the ICT familiarity questionnaire. They excluded cases with incomplete information on ENTUSE, HOMESCH, USESCH, reading enjoyment, reading metacognition, or reading literacy, resulting in an analytic sample of 5,164 students from 152 schools.

confounders_identified.variable_name: ICT use for schoolwork at home
ICT use for school at school

top_predictors: ICT use for school at school
ICT use for schoolwork at home
main_findings.performance_metrics: Multiple linear regression (n=5164): USESCH direct effect β=-7.106, t=-6.847, p<.001; Reading enjoyment β=27.710, t=15.832, p<.001; Reading metacognition β=54.159, t=37.258, p<.001. For HOMESCH direct effect β=-0.865, t=-0.721, p=.471 (not significant). For ENTUSE direct effect β=1.124, t=1.018, p=.309 (not significant).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Hong Kong the study leveraged ICT use for school at school (USESCH), reading enjoyment, and reading metacognition to predict reading literacy, finding that USESCH had a significant negative direct effect while reading enjoyment and reading metacognition had significant positive associations. This indicates that Hong Kong students’ reading performance is more strongly linked to metacognitive proficiency and enjoyment than to ICT use per se, and that ICT in school contexts may require pedagogical redesign to avoid undermining reading outcomes.

top_predictors: ICT use for school at school
ICT use for schoolwork at home
main_findings.performance_metrics: Multiple linear regression (n=5164): USESCH → reading enjoyment β=-0.009, t=-1.108, p=.268 (not significant). HOMESCH → reading enjoyment β=0.052, t=5.292, p<.001. ENTUSE → reading enjoyment β=-0.037, t=-4.122, p<.001.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Hong Kong the study leveraged ICT use for school at school, ICT use for schoolwork at home, and ICT use for entertainment to predict reading enjoyment, finding that HOMESCH positively predicted enjoyment while ENTUSE negatively predicted enjoyment and USESCH showed no significant relationship. This indicates that the motivational impact of ICT depends on purpose, suggesting that home-based schoolwork ICT may support reading enjoyment whereas entertainment-oriented ICT may erode it.

top_predictors: ICT use for school at school
ICT use for schoolwork at home
main_findings.performance_metrics: Multiple linear regression (n=5164): USESCH → reading metacognition β=-0.100, t=-10.150, p<.001. HOMESCH → reading metacognition β=-0.055, t=-4.752, p<.001. ENTUSE → reading metacognition β=-0.065, t=-6.197, p<.001. Reading enjoyment → reading metacognition β=0.313, t=19.309, p<.001.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Hong Kong the study leveraged ICT use for school at school, ICT use for schoolwork at home, and ICT use for entertainment to predict reading metacognition, finding that all three ICT-use types negatively predicted metacognition, while reading enjoyment strongly and positively predicted metacognition. This indicates that ICT use may be associated with weaker metacognitive regulation unless paired with enjoyment-supportive and metacognitive-training practices.

main_findings.target_variable: Serial multiple mediation: USESCH → reading enjoyment → reading metacognition → reading literacy
top_predictors: ICT use for school at school
main_findings.performance_metrics: PROCESS Model 6 with 5000 bootstrap samples: USESCH → reading enjoyment → reading literacy indirect effect β=-0.260, SE=0.235, 95% CI [0.037, 0.198] (reported as significant in Table 3 despite sign formatting); USESCH → reading metacognition → reading literacy indirect effect β=-5.410, SE=0.558, 95% CI [-6.500, -4.303]; USESCH → reading enjoyment → reading metacognition → reading literacy indirect effect β=-0.159, SE=0.143, 95% CI [0.022, 0.125]. Total indirect effect β=-5.828, SE=0.680, 95% CI [-7.153, -4.488]; total effect β=-12.934, SE=1.217, 95% CI [-15.320, -10.547].
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Hong Kong the study leveraged USESCH with reading enjoyment and reading metacognition as serial mediators to predict reading literacy, finding a significant negative mediation chain primarily through reading metacognition (and additional indirect paths reported via bootstrapped confidence intervals). This indicates that simply increasing ICT use in school may not improve reading literacy and may instead require metacognitive scaffolding and enjoyment-supportive instruction to protect reading regulation.

main_findings.target_variable: Serial multiple mediation: HOMESCH → reading enjoyment → reading metacognition → reading literacy
top_predictors: ICT use for schoolwork at home
main_findings.performance_metrics: PROCESS Model 6 with 5000 bootstrap samples: HOMESCH → reading enjoyment → reading literacy indirect effect β=1.424, SE=0.300, 95% CI [0.842, 2.026]; HOMESCH → reading metacognition → reading literacy indirect effect β=-3.033, SE=0.729, 95% CI [-4.444, -1.587]; HOMESCH → reading enjoyment → reading metacognition → reading literacy indirect effect β=-0.920, SE=0.193, 95% CI [0.552, 1.306] (as reported in Table 3). Total indirect effect β=-0.689, SE=0.892, 95% CI [-2.419, 1.046]; total effect β=-1.554, SE=1.424, 95% CI [-4.345, 1.237].
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Hong Kong the study leveraged HOMESCH with reading enjoyment and reading metacognition as serial mediators to predict reading literacy, finding that enjoyment positively mediated one pathway while metacognition negatively mediated another, producing a suppressing pattern across chains. This indicates that home ICT for schoolwork may support reading enjoyment but can still undermine metacognitive regulation unless learning activities are designed to foster strategic reading and self-monitoring.

main_findings.target_variable: Serial multiple mediation: ENTUSE → reading enjoyment → reading metacognition → reading literacy
main_findings.performance_metrics: PROCESS Model 6 with 5000 bootstrap samples: ENTUSE → reading enjoyment → reading literacy indirect effect β=-1.020, SE=0.259, 95% CI [-1.541, -0.529]; ENTUSE → reading metacognition → reading literacy indirect effect β=-3.642, SE=0.672, 95% CI [-4.953, -2.333]; ENTUSE → reading enjoyment → reading metacognition → reading literacy indirect effect β=-0.638, SE=0.159, 95% CI [-0.962, -0.323]. Total indirect effect β=-5.300, SE=0.815, 95% CI [-6.880, -3.672]; total effect β=-4.176, SE=1.309, 95% CI [-6.741, -1.610]. Direct effect ENTUSE → reading literacy β=1.124, SE=1.105, 95% CI [-1.041, 3.290] (not significant).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Hong Kong the study leveraged ENTUSE with reading enjoyment and reading metacognition as serial mediators to predict reading literacy, finding that the indirect effects were significantly negative across enjoyment and metacognition pathways while the direct effect was not significant. This indicates that entertainment-oriented ICT may harm reading literacy mainly by reducing reading enjoyment and weakening metacognitive regulation, supporting policies that balance leisure ICT with structured, enjoyment-enhancing reading experiences.

data.outcome_summary: This study analyzes the Hong Kong sample from PISA 2018 (n=5,164 students) to test how three ICT-use types (USESCH, HOMESCH, ENTUSE) relate to reading literacy, with reading enjoyment and reading metacognition as serial mediators. The authors used SPSS 25.0 and PROCESS Model 6 with 5,000 bootstrap resamples to estimate mediation paths, and they reported regression coefficients (e.g., USESCH direct effect on reading literacy β=-7.106, p<.001; reading enjoyment β=27.710, p<.001; reading metacognition β=54.159, p<.001). They also report bootstrapped indirect effects with 95% confidence intervals for multiple mediation chains, finding significant negative mediation for ENTUSE and a metacognition-driven negative mediation for USESCH. Limitations include cross-sectional design (no causal inference), reliance on self-report ICT/enjoyment/metacognition measures, and unclear use of PISA complex-sampling weights in the regression/mediation procedures.
